items.question: Methotrexate inhibits which enzyme?
items.explanation: Methotrexate inhibits dihydrofolate reductase, reducing folate and DNA synthesis; rescued by folinic acid.

items.question: Leucovorin (folinic acid) rescue is used after high-dose?
items.explanation: Folinic acid bypasses the DHFR block, rescuing normal cells after high-dose methotrexate.

items.question: Immune checkpoint inhibitors like nivolumab target?
items.explanation: Nivolumab/pembrolizumab block PD-1, restoring T-cell antitumour activity; can cause immune-related adverse effects.

items.question: Immune-related adverse effects of checkpoint inhibitors are treated with?
items.explanation: Checkpoint inhibitor colitis, pneumonitis and endocrinopathies are managed with corticosteroids.

items.question: Which antihypertensive is preferred in a diabetic with proteinuria?
items.explanation: ACE inhibitors/ARBs reduce intraglomerular pressure and proteinuria, slowing diabetic nephropathy.

*PharmaCraft Daily - 07 Nov 2026*

🎓 *MBBS* (Anticancer & Immuno)
Q: Methotrexate inhibits which enzyme?
Ans: Dihydrofolate reductase
Why: Methotrexate inhibits dihydrofolate reductase, reducing folate and DNA synthesis; rescued by folinic acid.

🌍 *FMGE* (Anticancer & Immuno)
Q: Leucovorin (folinic acid) rescue is used after high-dose?
Ans: Methotrexate
Why: Folinic acid bypasses the DHFR block, rescuing normal cells after high-dose methotrexate.

🩺 *NEET PG* (Anticancer & Immuno)
Q: Immune checkpoint inhibitors like nivolumab target?
Ans: PD-1
Why: Nivolumab/pembrolizumab block PD-1, restoring T-cell antitumour activity; can cause immune-related adverse effects.

🏥 *INI-CET* (Anticancer & Immuno)
Q: Immune-related adverse effects of checkpoint inhibitors are treated with?
Ans: Corticosteroids/immunosuppression
Why: Checkpoint inhibitor colitis, pneumonitis and endocrinopathies are managed with corticosteroids.

🔬 *MD Pharmacology* (Paper III: Systemic)
Q: Which antihypertensive is preferred in a diabetic with proteinuria?
Ans: ACE inhibitor/ARB
Why: ACE inhibitors/ARBs reduce intraglomerular pressure and proteinuria, slowing diabetic nephropathy.
